statement: A wall uses one of three structure types, each with its own settings and effect on junctions and quantities.

source.ref: Tool Settings Dialog Boxes > Wall Tool Settings

superiority: Structure type is a swap with automatic parameter mapping and report.

acceptance.sketch: Switch a wall between basic and composite: thickness stays consistent and junction cleanup re-evaluates.

notes: VERIFIED — read Wall Tool Settings; Wall Structure icons choose Basic, Composite or Complex Profile with a building material, composite or profile attribute.

statement: Reinforcement is documented by 2D details or library objects attached to columns and beams rather than analytical rebar.

source.ref: Column: reinforcement via attached details and symbols

superiority: Native parametric reinforcement with bar schedules.

acceptance.sketch: Attached detail follows the column when it moves.

notes: REJECTED: searched reinforcement and rebar across AC30 and MEP help; no reinforcement tool or bar schedule is documented (only generic 2D Detail Element objects such as steel profile and timber member symbols).

statement: Beams join other beams along their reference axes and meet columns and walls by geometric collision, with Building Material priority and junction order deciding which element cuts which.

source.ref: Element Intersections > Specific Element Intersections and Junctions

superiority: Declared joints with analytic checks.

acceptance.sketch: Beam end meets column face with no overlap volume.

notes: CORRECTED — read Specific Element Intersections and Junctions and Beams and Other Elements; slanted-join trimming is not described, joins of beam segments are set by a join angle (Define Join Geometry).

statement: Customize the edge angle and edge surface of individual slab edges and slab holes, and create holes by drawing a contour inside an existing slab.

source.ref: Slabs > Set Custom Slab Edge Angle and Edge Surface

superiority: Edge profiles shared with walls.

acceptance.sketch: Giving one edge of length L on a slab of thickness t a 45 degree custom angle changes the slab volume by t squared over 2 times L.

notes: CORRECTED — read Set Custom Slab Edge Angle and Edge Surface and Placing Holes in Slabs; edge profiles are not documented for slabs (profiles apply to walls, columns and beams), edge angle and surface are.

statement: Model footings as part of a wall by applying a complex profile that includes a footing section, for example a brick wall with footing.

source.ref: Construction Elements > Complex Profiles

superiority: Dedicated foundation objects with checks.

acceptance.sketch: A wall of length L using a profile whose footing region has area A has a footing component volume of A times L.

notes: CORRECTED — read Complex Profiles; only a 'Brick Wall with Footing' profile example is documented, no dedicated foundation or strip-footing settings on slabs, columns and beams.

statement: Create dormers and roof openings with library or profile-based shapes.

source.ref: Roof: dormer and skylight openings (Roof Accessories)

superiority: Dormer as parametric roof accessory.

acceptance.sketch: A dormer opening cuts the roof by the outline projected along the roof normal.

notes: REJECTED: no dormer or Roof Accessories feature in AC30 help; roofs offer holes (Create a Hole in a Roof), a roof tower and RoofMaker GDL parts for rafters, purlins and ridges instead.

statement: Trim a shell to a contour polygon drawn in plan or section, and edit that contour by offsetting, turning its plane, dragging, rotating or mirroring.

source.ref: Shells > Define Shell Contour

superiority: Join with continuity checking.

acceptance.sketch: A shell trimmed with a contour polygon parallel to the floor plan has a plan footprint whose area equals the polygon area within 1e-6.

notes: CORRECTED — read Define Shell Contour and Edit Shell Contour Polygon; joining shells to walls is done by separate trim and merge commands (Trim Elements to Roof or Shell), not by contour editing.

statement: Layer intersection numbers split elements into groups so that only elements whose layers share a number clean up against each other, in addition to Building Material priority.

source.ref: Element Intersections > Basic Intersection Principles

superiority: Group logic visible on screen.

acceptance.sketch: Two crossing walls on layers with different intersection numbers stay uncut, and with equal numbers they junction by material priority.

notes: CORRECTED — read Basic Intersection Principles; layers carry an intersection number used as a group tag, unrelated to element priorities.

statement: Only elements with a load-bearing structural function, the structural member option enabled and a core generate analytical members, so one flag drives analytical model membership.

source.ref: Structural Analytical Model > Elements of the Structural Analytical Model

superiority: Flag drives analysis and IFC consistently.

acceptance.sketch: Only elements flagged load-bearing generate analytical members.

notes: CORRECTED — read Elements of the Structural Analytical Model, 1D Members and 2D Members; conditions are load-bearing function, structural member checkbox, eligible tool (column, beam, wall, single-plane roof, slab) and a core component.

statement: List component volumes (net, gross or conditional), projected component areas, mass, embodied carbon and embodied energy per element component.

source.ref: Element Listing Parameters > Component Listing Parameters in the Interactive Schedule

superiority: Direct output to estimators.

acceptance.sketch: Net component volume of a wall equals gross volume minus opening volume, and component mass equals component volume times the material density.

notes: CORRECTED — read Component Listing Parameters in the Interactive Schedule; formwork area is not a documented parameter, volumes and projected areas are.

statement: Import standard steel profiles from a built-in database filtered by country code and geometry, and use them as complex-profile columns and beams that structural software recognises.

source.ref: Complex Profiles > Use Standard Steel Column or Beam Profile

superiority: Open catalogue in data files.

acceptance.sketch: A catalogue profile has area equal to the catalogue value within 0.1 percent.

notes: VERIFIED — read Use Standard Steel Column or Beam Profile; profile database imported via Options > Complex Profiles, listed by name in the interactive schedule.

statement: Timber members with grain direction and layered panels.

source.ref: Structural: Timber and CLT elements

superiority: Layered engineered timber elements with section properties.

acceptance.sketch: Layers of a CLT panel sum to total thickness and grain directions alternate.

notes: REJECTED: no timber, CLT, grain-direction or engineered-panel features in AC30 help (searched timber, CLT, layered panel); timber appears only as 2D detail element symbols and AI Visualizer prompts.

statement: Place opening elements (rectangular, circular or polygonal) in slabs and walls, and convert incoming IFC opening elements and provisions for void into native openings.

source.ref: Openings > Import/Save Openings with IFC

superiority: Penetration approval workflow.

acceptance.sketch: A circular opening of diameter d in a slab of thickness t removes a volume of pi d squared over 4 times t.

notes: CORRECTED — read Import/Save Openings with IFC and Create Opening; provisions for void arrive as classified morphs convertible to openings, approval workflow is not documented.

statement: Link two analytical members with a one-dimensional or surface link of a chosen type, so loads transfer between members without adjusting their geometry.

source.ref: Structural Analytical Model > Structural Links

superiority: Link types are checked for mechanisms and stiffness continuity.

acceptance.sketch: A zero-length 1D link between two braces connects their nodes, and moving either member moves the link with it.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Structural Links; links need two parent members and vanish if either parent is not in the current view.

statement: Manage load cases, each with an action type, load type and duration, inside load groups with a group type and relation, and import or export them as XML (import also from SAF).

source.ref: Structural Loads > Load Manager and Load Case/Group Settings

superiority: Cases and groups follow the selected design code with automatic default sets.

acceptance.sketch: Load case names are unique, and exporting then importing the XML reproduces every case and group with identical settings.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Load Manager, Load Case Settings, Load Group Settings and Load Case Palette; visible load case is stored per view.

statement: Place point force or moment, line (uniform or trapezoidal) and surface loads on analytical members with a load case, local or global coordinate system and edge-associative geometry.

source.ref: Structural Loads > Place Loads and Load Tool Settings

superiority: Loads are generated from rules and carry derived resultants for checks.

acceptance.sketch: A trapezoidal line load of 2 and 4 kN/m over 3 m has a total resultant of 9 kN.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Place Loads, Place Point Load, Place Line Load, Place Surface Load and Load Tool Settings.

statement: Generate surface live loads on zones by mapping zone classifications to load categories that hold unit values, and update them when zone geometry, classification or mapping changes.

source.ref: Structural Loads > Create/Update Live Loads

superiority: Occupancy loads follow the selected code table automatically.

acceptance.sketch: A 20 square metre zone mapped to a 3 kN per square metre category yields a 60 kN surface load, and changing the category value updates it.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Create/Update Live Loads and Set up Load Categories; categories import and export as XML.

statement: Apply ordered adjustment rules (offset, stretch, cutback, snap) with maximum distances between two member groups to connect analytical members into a continuous model without altering the physical model.

source.ref: Structural Analytical Model Generation Rules > Adjustment Rules

superiority: Rule effects are previewed live with a continuity report per rule.

acceptance.sketch: A beam axis 40 mm short of a column node connects under a 50 mm maximum stretch and stays disconnected under a 30 mm maximum.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Adjustment Rules, Set Up Adjustment Rules and Adjuster Types; rules apply only where cores connect and the element allows rule-based changes.

statement: Set translation and rotation release values (rigid, free or custom) at the ends of one-dimensional members and edges of two-dimensional members, with an export option that treats unconnected ends as rigid.

source.ref: Structural Analytical Model > End/Edge Releases

superiority: Release presets map to common connection types with checks against mechanisms.

acceptance.sketch: A member whose rotations are all free and translations rigid is displayed as a hinge and exports free rotation components, while the rigid override exports every unconnected end as rigid.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read End/Edge Releases and End/Edge Release (Generation Rules).

statement: Allow manual eccentricity or node edits of an analytical member relative to the element's center of gravity, which suspends global rules for that member until re-enabled or reverted.

source.ref: Structural Analytical Model > Eccentricity and Manual editing of analytical members

superiority: All manual edits are tracked as overrides with one-click revert.

acceptance.sketch: Dragging a member by 50 mm records an eccentricity of 50 mm and disables its offset rule, and revert restores the generated position.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Eccentricity and Manual editing of analytical members; manual edits work on one member at a time.

statement: Check the physical model before generating the analytical model for load-bearing elements lacking core connection, nearby gaps and inadequate core dimension ratios with adjustable tolerances.

source.ref: Model Check > Physical Model Quality Check

superiority: Checks run continuously with quick-fix commands.

acceptance.sketch: Two load-bearing elements 3 mm apart with a 5 mm tolerance appear in the report, and moving one to touch clears the item.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Physical Model Quality Check and Physical Model Check Parameters; results go to the Model Check Report.

statement: Check the analytical model for unconnected members, close nodes, overlaps, short members, small members and short consecutive edges with adjustable tolerances before export.

source.ref: Model Check > Structural Analytical Model Quality Check

superiority: Failures link to the rule or element setting that causes them.

acceptance.sketch: Two beams whose analytical members fully overlap with identical parameters are reported as duplicates, and deleting one clears the item.

notes: ADDED+VERIFIED — read Structural Analytical Model Quality Check; needs analytical model display on, one parameter also finds load-bearing elements with no member.
